props.gloss_en: the mishna: nor [may one go out] in a single [sandal] when there is no wound on his foot
hence, if there is a wound on his foot, he goes out [in a single sandal]
Rav Huna: he goes out [with the sandal] on the [foot] that has the wound
evidently he [Rav Huna] holds: a sandal is made on account of pain
Chiyya bar Rav: he goes out [with the sandal] on the [foot] that has no wound
evidently he [Chiyya bar Rav] holds: it is made on account of comfort
and the one that has the wound -- its wound testifies for it [why it is unshod]
and R' Yochanan too holds this [view] of Rav Huna
R' Yochanan to Rav Shemen bar Abba: give me my shoes; he gave him the right one; he said to him: you have made it a wound
R' Yochanan: as tefillin, so shoes
R' Yochanan: as tefillin are on the left, so shoes [are put on] on the left [first]
the baraita: when he puts on [shoes], he puts on the right and afterwards puts on the left
when he removes [them], he removes the left and afterwards the right
when he washes, he washes the right and afterwards the left
when he anoints, he anoints the right and afterwards the left
one who wishes to anoint his whole body anoints his head first
because it [the head] is king over all his limbs
Rav Yosef: now that it is taught so and R' Yochanan said so, whoever did this did [rightly] and whoever did that did [rightly]
Abaye: perhaps R' Yochanan had not heard this mishna [baraita], and had he heard it he would have retracted
Abaye: or else he heard it, and held that the halakha is not as that mishna
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: a God-fearing person fulfils both
and who is that? Mar breih deRabbana
how does he do it? he puts on the right and does not tie, puts on the left and ties, and then ties the right
Rav Ashi: I saw Rav Kahana, that he was not particular [about the order]

supports.gloss_en: ולא ביחיד בזמן שאין ברגלו מכה -- הא יש ברגלו מכה נפיק: the mishna's condition implies its converse
אלמא קסבר סנדל לשום צער עביד -- since he shods the wounded foot, the sandal is for pain
אלמא קסבר לשום תענוג עביד -- since he shods the healthy foot, the sandal is for comfort
דאמר ליה רבי יוחנן לרב שמן בר אבא: הב לי מסנאי; יהב ליה דימין; אמר ליה: עשיתו מכה -- the shod foot counts as the wounded one, as Rav Huna (kind svara under protest: an incident adduced as proof)

deflected_by.gloss_en: ודילמא כחייא בר רב סבירא ליה, והכי קאמר: עשית של שמאל מכה -- perhaps he holds as Chiyya bar Rav and meant: you have made the LEFT [unshod] foot a wound

supports.gloss_en: ואזדא רבי יוחנן לטעמיה -- being handed the right shoe first was a fault because, for him, shoes begin on the left
כתפילין כך מנעלין: מה תפילין בשמאל אף מנעלין בשמאל
סך ראשו תחילה, מפני שהוא מלך על כל איבריו
